## Purpose

The research-writing framework in this repository makes recurring literature
work executable: retrieve candidate papers, apply metadata-based screening,
produce a synthesis, assemble a source-linked draft, and optionally open a
review PR.

Quarto is the publication layer, not the agent orchestrator. The workflow remains
in LangGraph and runs independently of website rendering.

## Architecture

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    Search[Search] --> Screen[Screen]
    Screen --> Synthesize[Synthesize]
    Synthesize --> Store[Bundle]
    Store --> Publish[Review PR]
```

| Stage | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Search | Retrieve candidate metadata from arXiv and Semantic Scholar |
| Screen | Deduplicate and rank using venue, citation, and recency heuristics |
| Synthesize | Use the configured model, or deterministic no-LLM drafting |
| Bundle | Write a Quarto article, bibliography, source records, and social-copy sidecar |
| Publish | On explicit request, prepare a research-branch site change and open a PR |

## Autonomy and publication are separate

The configured workflow progresses through its stages without new approval
prompts between them. By default, it writes a local draft and performs no Git
publication. A requested non-dry run can open a PR containing the intended site
page, but it does not merge or deploy.

That boundary lets the research workflow remain autonomous without treating
unreviewed output as approved public content.

## Traceable artifacts

The source record travels alongside the draft. The publishing path checks an
explicit file set, protects existing destinations, and refuses unrelated Git
changes. The website build validates local links, bibliography resolution,
publication paths, and output boundaries without making model calls.

Tests exercise document serialization, filesystem boundaries, rendered
citations, temporary-repository publication, and the configured graph with
controlled retrieval inputs.

## Current limits

The present writer works from truncated abstracts and metadata. Its screening
scores are discovery heuristics, not scientific-quality assessments. A draft is
therefore labeled unverified. The framework does not currently implement or
validate original experiments, establish novelty, or certify its conclusions.

Future improvements can add full-text extraction, stronger source checking,
and new research stages while preserving explicit state and provenance.

## Using the framework

The repository includes an authoring handbook and setup instructions. Runtime
provider configuration supports Ollama and OpenAI. The optional agent dependency
group stays separate from the ordinary website build.
